Subject: Redwood Private VPC evaluation - networking & next tests

Hi Sanjay - thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side based on what we heard: 

Call recap:
- Goal: run a short Private/VPC PoC to validate network architecture, control-plane placement, and air-gap feasibility for sensitive PHI workloads.
- Key requirements: no egress of plaintext customer data, option for air-gapped on-prem bundle, SOC 2 evidence / audit logs, and predictable latency for HS model in VPC.
- Primary contacts: you (Sanjay), procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com), our engineering lead Camila for the deep-dive.

Redwood differentiators (brief):
- Private control plane option that can be customer-managed inside the customer VPC (no public-control-plane dependency).
- Offline / air-gapped on-prem bundle available for regulated environments (we've done this with two healthcare customers).
- High-throughput serving runtime with prefix/KV caching and quantization profiles to lower token cost without large quality regressions.
- Smart routing + fallbacks to ensure reliability if a node is degraded - important for predictable latency.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) You share the network diagram and egress constraints (we can start from a checklist) - I attached a short networking checklist and a Redwood vs hyperscaler comparison.
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/security and Camila (engineering) - we'll cover control-plane options and cert exchange.
3) Run a lightweight connectivity smoke test (SSH/TLS handshake + limited IP allowlist) to validate peering and NAT behavior.
4) We will compile SOC2 evidence and example audit logs for your GRC team.

Attachments: redwood-private-networking-checklist.pdf, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.xlsx

If that sounds right, I'll loop in Camila to book the deep-dive and Marissa for procurement conversations.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Subject: Fwd: Redwood Private VPC evaluation - technical notes + test plan

Quick internal note after Sanjay's clarifying questions - copying Marissa for procurement visibility.

Answers / plan from the engineering side (draft):
- Control plane: we support two deployment modes for the control plane:
  * Customer-managed control plane inside the customer VPC (preferred for Acme): all control-plane services run in their account/subnet; telemetry is optional and can be configured to route through a proxy.
  * Redwood-hosted control plane with VPC peering (less common for PHI).
- Air-gap/offline bundle: we provide an offline deployment artifact (installer + signed packages). Upgrades are handled by applying signed bundles; we can do a staged roll-forward controlled by the customer's infra team. We will document the upgrade/patch cadence and provide a signing policy.
- Networking: recommend initial smoke test items:
  1) TLS cert exchange and verification
  2) IP allowlist and NAT egress validation (verify no outbound to internet except allowed endpoints)
  3) Minimal latency/throughput check with a small model to validate cold-starts

Proposed test owners / timeline:
- Redwood: Camila (eng) lead for deep-dive and provide signed bundle + checklist
- Acme: Sanjay (platform) lead for network config and procurement will own contract steps

I'll draft a timeline in the meeting - suggest 1 week to schedule the deep-dive and 2 weeks for the initial smoke tests.

Camila

From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@cloudvendor.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Redwood Private VPC evaluation - control plane & air-gap details

Hi all - engineering note from the partner side to clarify how we've done this with other customers: 

- Control plane placement: yes, we've deployed Redwood's control plane entirely inside customer VPCs using a Helm/manifest-based deployment. No public control-plane endpoints are required. We configure a private ALB + security groups; optional S3 endpoints can be used for artifacts.
- Telemetry & cert rotation: telemetry can be disabled; cert rotation can be handled by a PKI workflow inside the VPC (we provide tooling for signed cert bundles).
- Air-gapped installs: we provide an "offline bundle" package for customers that cannot reach the public internet. The process we follow: export signed bundles from our build system, transfer via secure media, then run an on-site installer. Patching is manual (customer triggers install) or can be run by Redwood's infra engineers onsite under an MSA.

Recommended next test (minimal):
1) Establish VPC peering and allowlist only the installer artifact host (or perform manual transfer).
2) Run TLS handshake + cert validation test.
3) Validate that telemetry is enclosed (no outbound endpoints) by running a packet-capture during a smoke run.

Link to our airgap guide: https://drive.google.com/open?id=airgap-guide (we'll share the detailed PDF before the deep-dive).

Happy to join the deep-dive if you want a partner engineer present.

- Priya
Principal Solutions Architect
